messages:
Ravi (PM): intake: customers (Acme + Beta group) want a terse, machine- and human-readable "fallback_reason" per fallback decision. They want to show it in their dashboards and use it in alerts.
Nina (Eng): quick ask: do we prefer a single freeform string or a small structured payload? both have tradeoffs.
Ravi (PM): preference: structured minimal payload + a short, sanitized message for humans. Key constraints: no raw user prompts, no embeddings, and default retention aligned to platform logs.
Diego (CS): support note: tickets come in saying "fallback happened but we don't know why". If we can tag by cause (capacity|safety|quality|config|runtime_error) that's huge.
Ellie (SRE): infra constraints: router already evaluates fallbacks. Emitting per-request events will multiply volume. propose "one event per fallback decision" with optional aggregated counters. Also need per-tenant caps.
Kai (Research): we can populate quality_reason when we detect eval-metric drift > threshold. Provide a tiny summary: metric_name:delta. Example: "BLEU:-0.12". Keep it optional.
Ravi (PM): goals:
- provide fallback_event with fields: reason_code (enum), human_summary (<=120 chars), model_from, model_to, request_sample_count (if aggregated), event_time, request_ids (sampled)
- have opt-in for detailed_metrics (small vector of metric deltas)
- enforce privacy: no prompt text or user identifiers; tenant_id only
non-goals:
- not including raw logs or full prompts by default
- not building consumer-side UI (we deliver API + sample CSV)
success metrics:
- 50% drop in "unknown fallback" support tags within 60 days of GA
- <3% increase in storage for tenants who don't opt-in
acceptance criteria:
- on fallback, system emits an event to topic `events.fallback.v1` containing: reason_code, human_summary, model_from, model_to, tenant_id, event_time, sample_request_ids (optional)
- human_summary length <=120 and passes sanitizer (no prompt substrings, no email/phone-like tokens)
- detailed_metrics only emitted when tenant opt-in flag enabled; opt-in controlled via Console + API
- provide example API for Console: GET /tenants/{id}/fallbacks?start=&end=&reason=&limit=100
- docs include privacy checklist and opt-in flow
Nina (Eng): implementation sketch: router emits a compact struct to an internal sanitizer service which strips detectable PII and truncates tokens, then publishes to Kafka topic. A downstream aggregator will compute per-tenant hourly counters and store events in cold storage.
Ellie (SRE): sampling strategy: default: emit full event (no metrics) for every fallback; full detailed_metrics only for 0.5% of events + manual tenant opt-in. Also apply per-tenant 500 events/hour hard cap.
Diego (CS): suggested human_summary examples (safe copy):
- "Capacity hit: routed to smaller model to meet latency SLO."
- "Quality detect: model produced lower accuracy vs baseline; routing changed."
- "Policy limit: tenant exceeded dedicated capacity; downgraded to shared pool."
Ravi (PM): privacy escalation: if a customer asks for prompt examples, require signed addendum + automated redaction pipeline before export. No exceptions.
deploy-bot: staging deploy scheduled: branch "fallback-reasons" -> 2026-04-05T14:00:00Z; CI green.
Nina (Eng): timeline proposal:
- day 1-3: schema + sanitizer + unit tests
- day 4-8: router hook + publish pipeline + per-tenant cap enforcement
- day 9-12: aggregation + Console API + docs
- day 13-16: internal beta with 3 tenants; collect feedback
Ellie (SRE): add SLO: event available in Console within 45s for 95th percentile. Add to oncall runbook.
Ravi (PM): owners: PM Ravi, Eng lead Nina, SRE Ellie, CS Diego, Research Kai.
Nina (Eng): question: prefer event-per-fallback or aggregate-incident? we prefer event-per-fallback but dedupe similar fallbacks within 1s into one event to avoid storms.
Ravi (PM): agree on dedupe window 1s; core requirement is traceability to the triggering request ids (sampled).
Kai (Research): small follow-up: add an auto-severity float 0.0-1.0 for triage automation. Will propose formula in RFC.
Diego (CS): comms plan: CS will pilot with Acme + 3 other tenants; we'll provide opt-in instructions and privacy FAQ.
Ellie (SRE): remind: make sure the topic is monitored; noisy tenants get throttled and flagged automatically.
Ravi (PM): next step: Nina to post RFC in #eng-platform by EOD Friday with schema, sample payloads, privacy checklist, and sampling config. Diego to prepare customer opt-in email template. Ellie to add SLO entry.
Nina (Eng): will publish RFC.
Diego (CS): will draft outreach.
Ravi (PM): thanks all. closing thread; followups in RFC. :rocket:
